title: Coherent unit-normalized scalar comparison for unbounded derived global sections
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a site small in a universe containing all coefficients [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. For each sheaf of commutative rings $R$ on $\mathcal C$, use module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] and ordinary unbounded derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]; every complex of $R$-modules has a K-injective resolution [def-pur-kinjective-complex, prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist]. Put $\Gamma_R(M)=\operatorname{Hom}_{\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C)}(1,M_{ab})$, with its abelian group structure, and let $H_R=R\Gamma_R:D(R)\to D(\operatorname{Ab})$ have universal derived unit $\eta_R$ [def-sfb-right-derived-functor]. For $a:R\to S$, let $r_{R,S}:D(S)\to D(R)$ be termwise exact restriction of scalars [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars]. Under the underived equality $\Gamma_Rr_{R,S}=\Gamma_S$, there is a unique natural transformation
$$\sigma_{R,S}:H_S\longrightarrow H_Rr_{R,S},\qquad \sigma_{R,S,QM}\circ\eta_{S,M}=\eta_{R,r_{R,S}M}$$
for every complex $M$ of $S$-modules. This transformation is an isomorphism. It is the canonical derived direct-image composition comparison [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pushforward-composition] for the coefficient morphism $f:(\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C),S)\to(\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C),R)$, whose module direct image is restriction of scalars [lem-weil-pbc-restriction-ringed-topos-module-direct-image], followed by the global-sections ringed-topos morphism $g_R:(\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C),R)\to(\operatorname{Set},\mathbf Z)$ [def-weil-pbc-ringed-topos-morphism]. Here $\operatorname{Set}$ is presented by the one-object site with only its identity arrow and maximal covering sieve; the inverse image of $g_R$ is the constant-sheaf functor [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf], its direct image is global sections, and its structural ring map is $\underline{\mathbf Z}\to R$. Under the exact identification of $\mathbf Z$-modules on that singleton site with abelian groups [lem-weil-pbc-singleton-site-module-comparison], its module direct image is $\Gamma_R$. In particular, if $L$ is an $S$-K-injective complex and $j:r_{R,S}L\to K$ is an $R$-K-injective resolution, then $\Gamma(j)$ is a quasi-isomorphism and represents $\sigma_{R,S,QL}$ under the canonical resolution identifications. For every composable $R\to S\to T$, identifying the identical scalar actions $r_{R,S}r_{S,T}=r_{R,T}$, the same comparisons satisfy
$$\sigma_{R,T}=(\sigma_{R,S}r_{S,T})\circ\sigma_{S,T},\qquad \sigma_{R,R}=1_{H_R}.$$
All comparisons are natural in the derived module argument. No flatness or injective-preservation hypothesis on scalar restriction is imposed.

source.place: Tag 0D6E, lemma-derived-pushforward-composition; agent specializes to coefficient restriction followed by the global-sections ringed-topos morphism and fixes the comparison by universal derived units, including their composition law (former steps 5-6).

proof.text: Write C(r) for restriction on complexes and r for its descent to derived categories. Restriction leaves underlying abelian sheaves and all arrows unchanged. The sectionwise kernel and sheafified-cokernel descriptions therefore give the same kernels and cokernels before and after restriction, with restricted ring action. Thus C(r) preserves quasi-isomorphisms and descends by localization. The identical scalar actions give C(r_{R,S})C(r_{S,T})=C(r_{R,T}) and r_{R,R}=id, compatibly with localization. Moreover r itself, with identity unit, is a total right derived functor of C(r): both sides of its derived universal property are the natural transformations obtained by precomposition with localization. This is a bijection by the localization universal property. Hence the total derived direct image of an exact scalar restriction is canonically r, with this normalization. In Lean, exactness is reflected by the faithful forgetful functor to abelian sheaves; its preservation of colimits is supplied by moduleSheaves_colimits_forgetful. The formal presentation names the existing composition and identity isomorphisms of restriction, then lifts them termwise. Forgetful-sheaf identities lift through global sections and complexes to prove their compatibility.

source.place: Tag 0D6E: exact coefficient restriction specialization; localization universal property and derived-unit convention

proof.text: For a set E, a map from its constant presheaf to a sheaf F is exactly an E-indexed family of maps 1 to F, by taking the component at each e in E. Sheafification's adjunction therefore gives Hom(underline E,F)=Hom(E,Hom(1,F)). The constant-presheaf functor preserves finite limits objectwise, and set sheafification preserves finite limits, so their composite does also. This constructs the geometric morphism to Set, presented by the stated singleton site, without requiring a terminal object of C. The maps n to n times 1 in each R(U) commute with restrictions and extend uniquely from the constant presheaf Z to a ring-sheaf map underline Z to R. This supplies g_R as a ringed-topos morphism. Assemble the geometric adjunction and ring map as RingData and apply ringData_inducedModules. Evaluation on the punctual site gives the underlying-set comparison. Naturality with biproduct inclusions and projections makes this comparison additive, hence an isomorphism of abelian groups.

source.place: sites.tex, Tag 0H7J (example-constant-sheaf), Tag 06UN (definition-global-sections), Tag 00WJ (lemma-sheafification-exact); ringed structure as in Tag 01D3

proof.text: Use the coefficient ringed-topos morphism f supplied by the restriction/direct-image lemma. By the definition of module direct image, g_R sends M to Hom(1,M_ab), with its abelian operations and the usual integer action. Evaluation on the singleton site identifies this Z-module direct image with Gamma_R. The underlying geometric morphisms g_R f and g_S coincide; their structural maps agree since a(n times 1_R)=n times 1_S. Their module direct images are therefore Gamma_R C(r)=Gamma_S, including all maps. Apply the unbounded ringed-topos composition theorem to f followed by g_R. In particular, for S-K-injective L and any R-K-injective resolution j:C(r)L to K, Gamma(j) is a quasi-isomorphism; it represents kappa_{g_R,f,QL} with the theorem's canonical resolution identifications. The sites C and the singleton site are small in the common coefficient universe, so this theorem applies. The Lean proof uses exact evaluation directly: forget to abelian sheaves, use the bottom-topology equivalence with presheaves, and evaluate. Transport the quasi-isomorphism through the additive comparison; the general singleton tensor/derived equivalence is unnecessary.

source.place: Tag 0D6E (lemma-derived-pushforward-composition), coefficient morphism followed by g_R; canonical K-injective representative formula

proof.text: The natural family eta_{R,C(r)M}, using Gamma_R C(r)=Gamma_S and r Q_S=Q_R C(r), is a transformation Q_Ab Gamma_S to H_R r Q_S. Apply the bijection in the universal property of (H_S,eta_S), with G=H_R r. Its unique preimage is a natural transformation sigma_{R,S}:H_S to H_R r. By the defining bijection its components satisfy sigma_{R,S,Q_SM} eta_{S,M}=eta_{R,C(r)M} for every complex M. This proves existence and uniqueness with precisely the required normalization, before any invertibility assertion.

source.place: Agent unit normalization of the specialization of Tag 0D6E; def-sfb-right-derived-functor universal bijection

proof.text:
Let L be S-K-injective and choose an R-K-injective resolution j:C(r)L to K. Existence is guaranteed for this small ringed site. The derived units eta_{S,L} and eta_{R,K} are isomorphisms. Naturality of eta_R at j reads H_R(Q_R j) eta_{R,C(r)L}=eta_{R,K} Q_Ab Gamma(j). Thus the normalization from step 4 gives the explicit formula
sigma_{R,S,Q_SL}=H_R(Q_R j)^{-1} eta_{R,K} Q_Ab Gamma(j) eta_{S,L}^{-1}.
Here Q_R j is invertible by localization, and Q_Ab Gamma(j) is invertible by step 3's composition theorem. Every factor is therefore invertible. For an arbitrary S-complex M choose a K-injective resolution s:M to L. Since r is exact, Q_S s and its image under H_R r are invertible; naturality gives sigma_{Q_SM}=(H_R r)(Q_S s)^{-1} sigma_{Q_SL} H_S(Q_S s), so every component of sigma is invertible.

source.place: Tag 0D6E canonical resolution formula, combined with derived-unit naturality and K-injective resolutions; no preservation of K-injectives by r

proof.text: Identify Rf_* with r using the normalized exact-functor descent of step 1, and R(g_R f)_* with H_S using their identical underived functor and its derived unit. At S-K-injective L the source resolution identification is eta_{S,L}; at rL the target identification with Q_Ab Gamma(K) is eta_{R,K}^{-1} H_R(Q_R j). Consequently the resolution formula for kappa in step 3 gives exactly the formula for sigma in step 5. They agree on every Q_SL. Naturality at any K-injective resolution Q_S s, an isomorphism, gives equality at Q_SM; every derived object has a complex representative. Hence sigma is the canonical direct-image composition comparison, and Gamma(j) represents it under these canonical identifications. This also makes the representative formula independent of choices of j and K.

theorem derivedSectionsScalarCoherence
    [∀ R : Sheaf J CommRingCat.{u}, HasDerivedCategory.{w} (coefficientModules R)]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w} AddCommGrpCat.{u}] :
    (∀ R : Sheaf J CommRingCat.{u}, CoefficientSectionsGeometry R) ∧
    ∃ (H : ∀ R : Sheaf J CommRingCat.{u},
        DerivedCategory (coefficientModules R) ⥤ DerivedCategory AddCommGrpCat.{u})
      (η : ∀ R : Sheaf J CommRingCat.{u},
        coefficientComplexSections R ⋙ DerivedCategory.Q ⟶ DerivedCategory.Q ⋙ H R),
      (∀ R : Sheaf J CommRingCat.{u}, (H R).IsRightDerivedFunctor (η R)
        (HomologicalComplex.quasiIso (coefficientModules R) (ComplexShape.up ℤ))) ∧
      (∀ (R : Sheaf J CommRingCat.{u}) (I : CochainComplex (coefficientModules R) ℤ),
        I.IsKInjective → IsIso ((η R).app I)) ∧
      ∃ (r : ∀ {R S : Sheaf J CommRingCat.{u}}, (R ⟶ S) →
          DerivedCategory (coefficientModules S) ⥤ DerivedCategory (coefficientModules R))
        (ν : ∀ {R S : Sheaf J CommRingCat.{u}} (a : R ⟶ S),
          DerivedCategory.Q ⋙ r a ≅ coefficientComplexRestriction a ⋙ DerivedCategory.Q)
        (σ : ∀ {R S : Sheaf J CommRingCat.{u}} (a : R ⟶ S), H S ⟶ r a ⋙ H R),
        (∀ {R S : Sheaf J CommRingCat.{u}} (a : R ⟶ S),
          IsIso (σ a) ∧
          (∀ M : CochainComplex (coefficientModules S) ℤ,
            (η S).app M ≫ (σ a).app (DerivedCategory.Q.obj M) =
              DerivedCategory.Q.map ((coefficientComplexSectionsRestriction a).hom.app M) ≫
              (η R).app ((coefficientComplexRestriction a).obj M) ≫
                (H R).map ((ν a).inv.app M)) ∧
          (∀ τ : H S ⟶ r a ⋙ H R,
            (∀ M : CochainComplex (coefficientModules S) ℤ,
              (η S).app M ≫ τ.app (DerivedCategory.Q.obj M) =
                DerivedCategory.Q.map ((coefficientComplexSectionsRestriction a).hom.app M) ≫
                  (η R).app ((coefficientComplexRestriction a).obj M) ≫
                  (H R).map ((ν a).inv.app M)) → τ = σ a) ∧
          ∀ (I : CochainComplex (coefficientModules S) ℤ), I.IsKInjective →
          ∀ (K : CochainComplex (coefficientModules R) ℤ), K.IsKInjective →
          ∀ (j : (coefficientComplexRestriction a).obj I ⟶ K), ∀ [QuasiIso j],
            QuasiIso ((coefficientComplexSections R).map j) ∧
            (η S).app I ≫ (σ a).app (DerivedCategory.Q.obj I) ≫
              (H R).map ((ν a).hom.app I) ≫ (H R).map (DerivedCategory.Q.map j) =
                DerivedCategory.Q.map ((coefficientComplexSectionsRestriction a).hom.app I) ≫
                  DerivedCategory.Q.map ((coefficientComplexSections R).map j) ≫
                    (η R).app K) ∧
        (∀ {R S T : Sheaf J CommRingCat.{u}} (a : R ⟶ S) (b : S ⟶ T),
          ∃ c : r (a ≫ b) ≅ r b ⋙ r a,
            (∀ M : CochainComplex (coefficientModules T) ℤ,
              c.hom.app (DerivedCategory.Q.obj M) ≫
                (r a).map ((ν b).hom.app M) ≫
                  (ν a).hom.app ((coefficientComplexRestriction b).obj M) ≫
                    DerivedCategory.Q.map ((coefficientComplexRestrictionComp a b).hom.app M) =
                    (ν (a ≫ b)).hom.app M) ∧
            ∀ X : DerivedCategory (coefficientModules T),
              (σ (a ≫ b)).app X ≫ (H R).map (c.hom.app X) =
                (σ b).app X ≫ (σ a).app ((r b).obj X)) ∧
        ∀ R : Sheaf J CommRingCat.{u}, ∃ i : r (𝟙 R) ≅ 𝟭 _,
          (∀ M : CochainComplex (coefficientModules R) ℤ,
            i.hom.app (DerivedCategory.Q.obj M) = (ν (𝟙 R)).hom.app M ≫
              DerivedCategory.Q.map ((coefficientComplexRestrictionId R).hom.app M)) ∧
          ∀ X : DerivedCategory (coefficientModules R),
            (σ (𝟙 R)).app X ≫ (H R).map (i.hom.app X) = 𝟙 ((H R).obj X)
